# Extract structured data from a web page into JSON with a schema, and prove each field

**TL;DR** — To extract structured data from a web page into JSON with a schema and evidence, use a model for the extraction and xerj for the evidence. Schema-driven extraction in xerj is planned (issue #1797). Today it indexes saved pages and checks each field: on 2026-10-19, 4 of 5 fields were found, 1 flagged.

## Commands

### Command 1

Note: Start a single-user node on localhost:9200 in its own terminal.

```sh
xerj --insecure --data-dir ./xerj-data
```

### Command 2

Note: Index the saved HTML: tables become one record per row, prose becomes sections.

```sh
xerj autoindex ./pages --prefix web
```

### Command 3

Note: Run one match_phrase per extracted field and print found, source and evidence.

```sh
bash verify.sh
```

## What works today and what is planned

| Step | Status in v1.0.0-rc.97 |
| --- | --- |
| Index saved HTML, one document per table row | works |
| Find the passage a field came from, with file and section | works |
| Flag a field that is not in the source | works, with a script like the one below |
| Text plus JSON schema in, JSON out, source passage per field | planned, issue #1797 (open) |
| Fetch the page | not planned; save it yourself |

## Run it

Save the pages, index the folder, then check the fields your model returned. This run used four pages saved on 2026-10-19: xerj.org/pricing, xerj.org/security, xerj.org/docs/install and hub.xerj.org/about.

```sh
mkdir pages
curl -s https://xerj.org/pricing -o pages/xerj_org_pricing.html
curl -s https://xerj.org/security -o pages/xerj_org_security.html
xerj autoindex ./pages --prefix web
```

The index took 0.9 s and held 20 documents. Tables landed in `web-html`, one document per row:

```json
{"gate":"G1 domain","what_satisfies_it":"the row finishes \"an agent working on ___ would query this for ___\" in one specific sentence","ax_path":"hub_xerj_org_about.html","ax_locator":"row1","ax_format":"html"}
```

Here is what a model claimed it extracted, as JSON:

```json
{"pricing_unit": "per-node",
 "usage_fees": "No per-doc, per-vector, or per-query fees",
 "compliance_addon": "HIPAA BAA",
 "free_trial": "14-day free trial",
 "telemetry": "makes no runtime telemetry"}
```

`verify.sh` sends one `match_phrase` query per field to the node and prints what it found:

```sh
jq -r 'to_entries[] | "\(.key)\t\(.value)"' claims.json | while IFS=$'\t' read -r field value; do
  q=$(jq -nc --arg v "$value" '{size:1, _source:["ax_path","ax_locator","body"], query:{match_phrase:{body:$v}}}')
  curl -s 'localhost:9200/web-*/_search' -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$q" |
  jq -c --arg f "$field" --arg v "$value" '.hits.hits[0]._source as $s
    | if $s then {field:$f, found:true, source:"\($s.ax_path)#\($s.ax_locator)"}
      else {field:$f, found:false} end'
done
```

The full script also prints 40 characters either side of the match. Real output:

```text
{"field":"pricing_unit","value":"per-node","found":true,"source":"xerj_org_pricing.html#s0","evidence":" · Terraform module PER-NODE CONTACT FOR QUOTE → TIER 03 ENTERPRISE Multi-region · r"}
{"field":"usage_fees","value":"No per-doc, per-vector, or per-query fees","found":true,"source":"xerj_org_pricing.html#s2","evidence":"custom for Enterprise. No per-doc, per-vector, or per-query fees. Self-hosted means you own your compute. TALK TO SALES "}
{"field":"compliance_addon","value":"HIPAA BAA","found":true,"source":"xerj_org_pricing.html#s1","evidence":"SM + solutions architect HIPAA BAA · custom compliance Private roadmap inp"}
{"field":"free_trial","value":"14-day free trial","found":false,"source":null,"evidence":null}
{"field":"telemetry","value":"makes no runtime telemetry","found":true,"source":"xerj_org_security.html#s3","evidence":". RUNTIME BOUNDARY The running binary makes no runtime telemetry, update, or license-activation calls. T"}
```

The free-trial claim is not on either page, so the check flags it instead of passing it through.

## Measured on 2026-10-19

| Measure | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Pages indexed | 4 saved HTML files |
| Index time | 0.9 s, 20 documents |
| Fields checked | 5 |
| Found with file and section | 4 |
| Flagged as not in the source | 1 |
| Wall time for all 5 checks | 58 ms |

## How it compares

| Approach | Schema in, JSON out | Evidence per field | Runs locally | Fetches pages |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| xerj today | no, planned in #1797 | yes, file and section | yes | no |
| A model alone | yes | no, it can invent a value | depends | no |
| A scraping library | you write the selectors | the selector is the evidence | yes | yes |
| A hosted extraction API | yes | varies by vendor | no | yes |

## When not to use xerj

- You need the JSON filled for you from a schema today. That is #1797, still open.
- You extract from one page once. Reading it is quicker than indexing it.
- The value is not written verbatim on the page, such as a computed total. A phrase check cannot prove a number the page never prints.
- You must fetch, render or log in to the page. xerj indexes files you already saved.

## FAQ

### Can xerj extract structured data from a web page into a JSON schema?

Not yet. Schema in, JSON out, with a source passage per field, is open as issue #1797. Today xerj indexes the saved page and lets you check each field a model extracted.

### How do I verify an extracted field exists in the source text?

Index the saved pages with `xerj autoindex`, then run one `match_phrase` query per field value. A hit gives the file and section locator and the text around the match; no hit means flag the field.

### Does it turn HTML tables into JSON?

Yes. In our run a table on hub.xerj.org/about became one record per row, with fields named after the header cells (`gate`, `what_satisfies_it`) and locators `row1` to `row7`.

### Does xerj fetch the page for me?

No. Save the pages first with curl or a browser, then index the folder. xerj reads the files on disk; it has no crawler.

### Which small model should do the extraction?

Any model you already run. xerj does not ship an extraction model; it gives the model a smaller passage to read and gives you a check on what it returned.

### Can I see the matched words highlighted?

Not in our run. The `highlight` request returned nothing on rc.97, so the check script cuts the evidence window out of the body itself.
